pub fn promote_completed_run(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    state: &mut PipelineState,
) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    promote_completed_run_with_hook(paths, state, |_, _| Ok(()))
}

fn promote_completed_run_with_hook(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    state: &mut PipelineState,
    mut hook: impl FnMut(PromotionCheckpoint, &Path) -> Result<()>,
) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    let strict = is_strict_job(paths, state);
    let library_dir = paths.library_dir(&state.scope, &state.run_id);
    let parent = library_parent(&library_dir)?;
    let staging = legacy_staging_path(parent, &state.run_id);
    let candidate = sanitized_staging_path(parent, &state.run_id);
    let recovery_artifact_exists = library_dir.exists() || staging.exists() || candidate.exists();
    if strict && recovery_artifact_exists {
        // Older versions could publish (and even remove the run-owned
        // workspace) before saving state. Validate the existing candidate or
        // library through strict recovery first instead of requiring the stale
        // `working_dir` to remain readable.
        recover_promotion_with_hook(paths, state, &mut hook)?;
        validate_completion_receipt(paths, state)?;
    } else {
        if strict {
            validate_completion_receipt(paths, state)?;
        } else {
            validate_acceptance_marker(state)?;
        }
        recover_promotion_with_hook(paths, state, &mut hook)?;
    }
    if library_dir.exists() {
        return Ok(library_dir);
    }

    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
    if !state.working_dir.exists() {
        return Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!(
            "working directory {}",
            state.working_dir.display()
        )));
    }
    if staging.exists() {
        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
            "legacy promotion staging {} remains after recovery",
            staging.display()
        )));
    }
    let codebase = promotion_codebase_record(paths, state, &state.working_dir, false)?;
    let source_working_dir = expected_source_working_dir(state, &codebase)?;
    prepare_candidate(
        state,
        &codebase,
        &state.working_dir,
        &source_working_dir,
        &candidate,
    )?;
    hook(PromotionCheckpoint::CandidateReady, &candidate)?;
    validate_strict_candidate(paths, state, &candidate)?;
    hook(PromotionCheckpoint::CandidateValidated, &candidate)?;
    publish_candidate(&candidate, &library_dir)?;
    hook(PromotionCheckpoint::Published, &library_dir)?;
    validate_strict_candidate(paths, state, &library_dir)?;
    hook(PromotionCheckpoint::PublishedValidated, &library_dir)?;
    finalize_published_library(state, &library_dir, &codebase, &mut hook)?;
    remove_temporary_tree(&staging)?;
    remove_temporary_tree(&candidate)?;

pub fn prepare_worktree_record(
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    options: WorktreeOptions,
) -> Result<CodebaseRecord> {
    let git_root = find_git_root(&options.source_path)?.ok_or_else(|| {
        user_error(
            &format!("{} is not a git repo", options.source_path.display()),
            "git init or pass --from .",
        )
    })?;
    let base_ref = options
        .base_ref
        .unwrap_or_else(|| current_branch(&git_root).unwrap_or_else(|_| "HEAD".to_string()));
    preflight_worktree(&git_root, &base_ref, options.allow_dirty)?;
    let branch_name = options.branch_name.unwrap_or_else(|| {
        format!(
            "dr/{}-{}",
            options.task_key.chars().take(32).collect::<String>(),
            options.run_id.chars().take(8).collect::<String>()
        )
    });
    if git_ref_exists(&git_root, &branch_name)? {
        return Err(user_error(
            &format!("branch {branch_name} already exists"),
            "pass --branch-name <other-name>",
        ));
    }
    let scope = workspace_scope(&git_root)?;
    let worktree_path = unique_worktree_path(paths, &scope, &options.run_id);
    let base_sha = git_stdout(&git_root, &["rev-parse", &base_ref])?;
    let mut record = CodebaseRecord::fresh();
    record.mode = CodebaseMode::Worktree;
    record.source_path = Some(canonical_or_self(&options.source_path)?);
    record.source_git_root = Some(git_root);
    record.branch_name = Some(branch_name);
    record.base_ref = Some(base_ref);
    record.base_sha = Some(base_sha);
    record.worktree_path = Some(worktree_path);
    record.dirty_files_seeded = options.allow_dirty;
    Ok(record)
}

pub fn create_worktree(record: &CodebaseRecord) -> Result<()> {
    if record.mode != CodebaseMode::Worktree {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let git_root = required_path(record.source_git_root.as_ref(), "source_git_root")?;
    let worktree_path = required_path(record.worktree_path.as_ref(), "worktree_path")?;
    let branch = required_string(record.branch_name.as_deref(), "branch_name")?;
    let base = required_string(record.base_ref.as_deref(), "base_ref")?;
    if let Some(parent) = worktree_path.parent() {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
    }
    git_status(
        git_root,
        &[
            "worktree",
            "add",
            "-b",
            branch,
            path_str(worktree_path)?,
            base,
        ],
    )?;
    append_git_exclude(git_root, ".deadreckon/")?;
    if record.dirty_files_seeded {
        seed_dirty_files(git_root, worktree_path)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn copy_source_to_working(source: &Path, working_dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    if !source.exists() {
        return Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!(
            "source {}",
            source.display()
        )));
    }
    for entry in ignore::WalkBuilder::new(source)
        .hidden(false)
        .parents(true)
        .git_ignore(true)
        .git_global(true)
        .git_exclude(true)
        .follow_links(false)
        .build()
        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
    {
        let path = entry.path();
        if path == source || ignored_copy_path(source, path) {
            continue;
        }
        let relative = path.strip_prefix(source).unwrap_or(path);
        let dest = working_dir.join(relative);

pub fn write_codebase_record(working_dir: &Path, record: &CodebaseRecord) -> Result<()> {
    let path = codebase_record_path(working_dir);
    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("codebase record has no parent: {}", path.display()))
    })?;
    std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
    std::fs::write(
        &path,
        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(record).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
            path: path.clone(),
            source,
        })?,
    )
    .with_path(path)
}

pub fn read_codebase_record(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<CodebaseRecord> {
    let path = codebase_record_path(working_dir);
    let data = std::fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&data).with_json_path(path)
}

/// Persist the lifecycle routing record outside the agent-visible workspace.
///
/// The workspace copy remains useful to docs and legacy commands, but delivery
/// and receipt code should prefer this control-plane copy so a provider cannot
/// redirect `finish` by editing `.deadreckon/codebase.json`.
pub fn write_trusted_codebase_record(run_root: &Path, record: &CodebaseRecord) -> Result<()> {
    let path = run_root.join(TRUSTED_CODEBASE_RECORD);
    std::fs::write(
        &path,
        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(record).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
            path: path.clone(),
            source,
        })?,
    )
    .with_path(path)
}

pub fn read_trusted_codebase_record(run_root: &Path) -> Result<CodebaseRecord> {
    let path = run_root.join(TRUSTED_CODEBASE_RECORD);
    let data = std::fs::read(&path).with_path(&path)?;
    serde_json::from_slice(&data).with_json_path(path)
}

pub fn read_run_codebase_record(run_root: &Path, working_dir: &Path) -> Result<CodebaseRecord> {
    read_trusted_codebase_record(run_root).or_else(|error| {
        if matches!(
            &error,
            DeadreckonError::Io { source, .. }
                if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound
        ) {
            read_codebase_record(working_dir)
        } else {
            Err(error)
        }
    })
}

pub fn find_git_root(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<PathBuf>> {
    let output = run_git(path, &["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"])?;
    if !output.status.success() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let root = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();

                assert!(quiet);

+            materialize_verified_completed_run(

+                &state,

+                dest.clone(),

+fn read_verified_export_transaction(
+    path: &Path,
+    authority: &VerifiedDeliveryAuthority,
+) -> Result<VerifiedExportTransaction> {
+    let before = fs::symlink_metadata(path)?;
+    if !before.file_type().is_file() || before.file_type().is_symlink() {
+        return Err(verified_export_refusal(
+            authority,
+            "trusted export transaction journal is not a regular file",
+        ));
+    }
+    let raw = fs::read(path)?;
+    let after = fs::symlink_metadata(path)?;
+    if !same_verified_file_identity(&before, &after) {
+        return Err(verified_export_refusal(
+            authority,
+            "trusted export transaction journal changed while it was read",
+        ));
+    }
+    Ok(serde_json::from_slice(&raw)?)
+}
+
+#[cfg(unix)]
+fn same_verified_file_identity(left: &fs::Metadata, right: &fs::Metadata) -> bool {
+    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt as _;
+
+    left.file_type().is_file()
+        && right.file_type().is_file()
+        && left.dev() == right.dev()
+        && left.ino() == right.ino()
+        && left.len() == right.len()
+        && left.mtime() == right.mtime()
+        && left.mtime_nsec() == right.mtime_nsec()
+        && left.ctime() == right.ctime()
+        && left.ctime_nsec() == right.ctime_nsec()
+}
+
+#[cfg(not(unix))]
+fn same_verified_file_identity(left: &fs::Metadata, right: &fs::Metadata) -> bool {
+    left.file_type().is_file()
+        && right.file_type().is_file()
+        && left.len() == right.len()
+        && left.modified().ok() == right.modified().ok()
+}
+
+fn regular_file_sha256_if_present(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<String>> {
+    match fs::symlink_metadata(path) {
+        Ok(metadata)
+            if metadata.file_type().is_file() && !metadata.file_type().is_symlink() =>
+        {
+            Ok(Some(deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(path)?))
+        }
+        Ok(_) => Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
+            "verified export metadata is not a regular file: {}",
+            path.display()
+        )))),
+        Err(source) if source.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
+        Err(source) => Err(CliError::Io(source)),
+    }
+}

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-31 02:34:28Z)**_

Implemented verified export/materialize crash atomicity and TOCTOU closure in `crates/deadreckon/src/commands/lifecycle.rs`. No commit created.

Causal fix:

- Verified authority now retains and revalidates the exact signed receipt and receipt-file digest.
- Output is copied into a private sibling stage, fsynced, and checked against the signed result-tree identity.
- Forced overwrite uses a recoverable two-rename transaction with an exact prior-destination backup.
- Receipt, source manifest, staged tree, canonical destination, and published tree are revalidated.
- Publication failures restore the previous destination.
- `ResultExported` is recorded before backup cleanup.
- `.materialized-to` and delivery events are idempotent.
- Existing published output is recognized on retry, including stale-journal crash windows.
- Unexpected destination, stage, backup, journal, symlink, or parent-directory identities fail closed without cleanup.

Journal:

- Location: `~/.deadreckon/jobs/<job-id>/export-transactions/<transaction-id>.json`
- Transaction ID binds schema, Job/Run, normalized canonical destination, exact receipt digest, signed result-tree digest, and manifest option.
- Journal additionally binds parent inode/path identity, optional manifest digest, exact previous destination identity, derived stage/backup paths, and phase.
- Writes and directory/tree publication boundaries are fsynced.
- Recovery derives truth from validated filesystem state rather than trusting a possibly stale phase.

Tests added with real HMAC-signed receipts:

- public Job export success and factual delivery;
- post-validation source mutation refusal;
- no destination mutation on signed-receipt refusal;
- crash immediately after publication, before event;
- retry and duplicate-retry convergence;
- stale-journal recovery after backup rename and event append;
- staging symlink substitution refusal;
- canonical destination aliases;
- `materialize`, `export`, and `copy-out` parsing parity.

Verification:

- Focused verified-export suite: 5 passed.
- Public alias parser: 1 passed.
- Signed preflight refusal: 1 passed.
- Signed public export baseline: 1 passed.
- Lifecycle integration suite: 86 passed.
- `rustfmt` and `git diff --check`: clean.

<section id="design-decisions"><h2>Design decisions</h2><p>Wall-clock fixture writes notes before sleeping.</p></section>

# Unmet-Needs Options — 2026-07-01

**Subject:** what to build next so deadreckon keeps solving the class of unmet
needs it was born from.
**Method:** the original 25-needs research report
(`/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md`), re-scored
through the 2026-05-11 audit (`docs/AUDIT-2026-05-11.md`) and the v0.4.0
as-built, crossed with two `/last30days` research passes (2026-06-25: community
pain points, 116 items; 2026-07-01: harness capability shifts, 62 items) plus
targeted web supplements on Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode June-2026 releases
and the memory/evals tooling landscape.
**Status:** options catalog, not commitments. Each option names the need(s) it
serves, the demand evidence, the existing seam it plugs into, and a
build-effort read. Sequencing recommendation at the end.

---

## 1. Where deadreckon stands against its origin needs (post-v0.4.0)

v0.4.0 ("Honest verification", 2026-06-27) landed Polyglot done-contract
detection and the `verdict` verb. Against the original 25 needs:

| Movement | Needs |
|---|---|
| Newly strengthened by v0.4.0 | #14 Structural Verification (gate now non-hollow on 11 project kinds); #8/#24 Observability & Evals (verdict = re-runnable per-run eval); #6 Cross-Tool State (imported runs now get verdicts) |
| Resolved earlier, holding | #1 spend meter, #3 undo, #4 provenance, #5 team memory (library), #9 sandboxes, #11 permissions, #13 onboarding docs, #15 discoverability, #16 provider routing, #19 receipts, #21 local-first |
| Still partial | #7 desktop/diff UI, #8 eval dashboards/RCA, #10 richer budget guardrails, #17 human-agent handoff, #18 port/env isolation for parallel agents, #23 team standards (rules goal drafted, unexecuted), #24 efficiency evals, #25 run queue |
| Still V1 / untouched | **#2 multi-agent worktree coordination (fork verb)** — the top coordination need, V1 across every audit; #12 MCP setup & tooling debugger; #20 AI-review continuity; #22 meeting-to-code |

One drafted goal is ready to execute with no further research:
**Rules-as-gate** (`docs/goals/2026-06-25-1423-deadreckon-rules-gate-goal.md`),
serving needs #23 and #19.

## 2. What moved in the harness landscape in the last 30 days

The competitive context shifted materially this month; several of deadreckon's
"V1 someday" items are now table stakes elsewhere, while deadreckon's core
differentiator (the signed, tamper-evident gate) remains unmatched.

- **Claude Code (June 2026):** hierarchical subagent spawning to 3 levels with
  `--verbose-agents` delegation tracing; **agent checkpointing** (save/resume
  agent-tree state, beta); **per-agent, per-task cost attribution**; scoped
  least-privilege permissions on subagents; background subagents that surface
  permission prompts instead of auto-denying; Sonnet 5 default with 1M context.
- **Codex CLI (June 2026):** a **Goals system** (v0.128+) — persisted,
  multi-day, stateful-across-restarts workflows; manager/worker subagent
  orchestration with consolidated fan-in; browser execution via Chrome
  extension.
- **OpenCode:** background subagents that keep working while you do other
  things; a Scout repo-research agent; a Tauri desktop app; 75+ providers.
- **Ecosystem:** the "harness engineering" frame went mainstream ("Agent =
  Model + Harness … the harness is ~90% of it" — a team moved from outside
  top-30 to top-5 on a benchmark changing only the harness). Skill/agent packs
  exploded (agent-skills, 100+ subagent collections, auto-installer plugins),
  which is creating a **skills supply-chain risk** conversation (malicious
  skills/hooks pulled straight from GitHub). Memory tooling matured (Mem0
  benchmark report; TeleMem; AccInt — outcome-scored memory exposed to Claude
  Code/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor **via MCP**). Evals moved toward automated
  failure RCA (detectors over execution traces: "from 'test failed' to
  'here's what to fix'"). Token-efficiency tooling has real demand (Headroom's
  60–95% token-cut post: 2,616 upvotes, r/claudeskills). Session handoff
  between harnesses is being solved with ad-hoc skills (r/claudeskills,
  2026-06-02). Cross-session amnesia remains the loudest day-to-day complaint
  ("every new session forgetting your project is the real bottleneck" —
  279K-view TikTok).

//! Persisted wire vocabulary for trusted operator capture sessions.

use std::{collections::BTreeMap, num::NonZeroU64};

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use schemars::JsonSchema;
use schemars::schema::{InstanceType, Schema, SchemaObject};
use serde::de::Error as _;
use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::{JobId, JobShape};

/// The only operator-capture wire version understood by this release.
pub const OPERATOR_CAPTURE_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1;

/// Checked discriminator for every persisted operator-capture artifact.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize)]
#[serde(transparent)]
pub struct OperatorCaptureSchemaVersion(u32);

impl OperatorCaptureSchemaVersion {
    pub const CURRENT: Self = Self(OPERATOR_CAPTURE_SCHEMA_VERSION);

    pub const fn get(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for OperatorCaptureSchemaVersion {
    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
    where
        D: Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        let version = u32::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        if version == OPERATOR_CAPTURE_SCHEMA_VERSION {
            Ok(Self::CURRENT)
        } else {
            Err(D::Error::custom(format!(
                "unsupported operator capture schema version {version}; expected \
                 {OPERATOR_CAPTURE_SCHEMA_VERSION}"
            )))
        }
    }
}

impl JsonSchema for OperatorCaptureSchemaVersion {
    fn schema_name() -> String {
        "OperatorCaptureSchemaVersion".to_string()
    }

    fn json_schema(_generator: &mut schemars::r#gen::SchemaGenerator) -> Schema {
        Schema::Object(SchemaObject {
            instance_type: Some(InstanceType::Integer.into()),
            enum_values: Some(vec![Value::from(OPERATOR_CAPTURE_SCHEMA_VERSION)]),
            ..SchemaObject::default()
        })
    }

    fn is_referenceable() -> bool {
        false
    }
}

/// Immutable identity approved before the first capture event.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct OperatorCaptureBinding {
    pub schema_version: OperatorCaptureSchemaVersion,

}

    pub const fn new(value: u64) -> Option<Self> {

}

impl From<OperatorCaptureEventSequence> for u64 {
    fn from(value: OperatorCaptureEventSequence) -> Self {
        value.get()

}

+/// Replace one controller-owned JSON projection and append the event that
+/// authorizes that exact replacement while holding the Job control lock.
+///
+/// The projection is written first. A crash before the event therefore leaves
+/// an uncommitted projection that consumers must refuse as authority. Once the
+/// event is durable, lease reclamation cannot interleave with either write.
+pub fn replace_fenced_job_json_and_append_event<T: serde::Serialize>(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    token: &LeaseToken,
+    now: DateTime<Utc>,
+    artifact_path: &std::path::Path,
+    kind: JobEventKind,
+    causation_id: String,
+    detail: Value,
+    value: &T,
+) -> Result<JobProjection> {
+    let job_dir = paths.job_dir(token.job_id.as_ref());
+    let relative_artifact = artifact_path.strip_prefix(&job_dir).map_err(|_| {
+        lease_error(
+            &token.job_id,
+            "fenced artifact path is outside the protected Job directory",
+        )
+    })?;
+    if relative_artifact.as_os_str().is_empty()
+        || relative_artifact
+            .components()
+            .any(|component| !matches!(component, std::path::Component::Normal(_)))
+    {
+        return Err(lease_error(
+            &token.job_id,
+            "fenced artifact path is not a normalized protected Job child",
+        ));
+    }
+    let lock_path = job_dir.join(JOB_CONTROL_LOCK);
+    let lock = open_job_control_lock(&lock_path)?;
+    FileExt::lock_exclusive(&lock).with_path(&lock_path)?;
+
+    let lease = load_job_lease(paths, &token.job_id)?;
+    validate_token(&lease, token, now)?;
+    let history = read_job_history(&paths.job_events(token.job_id.as_ref()))?;
+    let projection = reduce_job_history(&token.job_id, &history)?;
+    if projection.is_terminal()
+        || projection.stop_reason == Some(deadreckon_protocol::StopReason::CancelRequested)
+    {
+        return Err(lease_error(
+            &token.job_id,
+            "cannot replace a fenced artifact after the Job stopped",
+        ));
+    }
+    let sequence = projection
+        .last_sequence
+        .checked_add(1)
+        .and_then(JobEventSequence::new)
+        .ok_or_else(|| lease_error(&token.job_id, "job event sequence exhausted"))?;
+    let event = JobEvent {
+        schema_version: JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT,
+        job_id: token.job_id.clone(),
+        sequence,
+        event_id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
+        causation_id,
+        timestamp: now,
+        lease_epoch: token.epoch,
+        kind,
+        detail,
+    };
+    atomic_write_json(artifact_path, value)?;
+    append_job_event_locked(paths, &event)
+}

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-31 03:10:47Z)**_

The core Watchkeeper idea is now implemented. What is not complete is integration of the newest hardening work and real-world proof that the whole promise survives hostile operating conditions.

## What is already integrated on `main`

There are 16 Watchkeeper commits from `79bb2e8` through `ad8d12c`. Local `main` matches the locally recorded `origin/main`.

Implemented:

- One durable `Job` identity with immutable authority, append-only history, fenced leases and typed terminal outcomes.
- Detached execution: `start` persists the Job before returning.
- Recovery machinery for worker and supervisor interruption without silently duplicating attempts.
- Explicit outcomes for verified, blocked, cancelled, needs-review, budget exhaustion, deadlines, retry exhaustion and failure.
- Bounded spend, wall-time and attempt policies.
- Two-key completion:
  1. deterministic checks must pass;
  2. an independent read-only semantic judge must return `achieved`.
- `revise` can initiate bounded additional work; `uncertain`, malformed or unavailable judgment becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`.
- HMAC-SHA-256 markers and receipts, with signing material outside the agent workspace.
- Receipts bound to the goal, contract, policy, source, result, revisions, proof evidence and containment.
- Crash-guarded gate evaluation and promotion.
- Supported direct runs, orchestrations, new chains, stored-plan forks and campaigns routed through the durable Job scheduler.
- Graph and Campaign parent verification.
- Bounded parent-only semantic repair without rerunning successful leaves.
- Job-aware `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list` and `finish`.
- A 24-task dogfood matrix, metrics machinery and credential-free adversarial tests.
- Clean committed adversarial evidence: 11 passes and 0 failures, while explicitly leaving live claims unproven.

That means the deterministic gate, semantic second key, durable scheduler and cryptographic receipt are no longer proposals. They exist in the integrated code.

## What has been built but is not integrated

A second large tranche currently sits unstaged in the shared `main` working tree:

- 62 modified product files.
- 10,156 tracked insertions and 737 deletions.
- Roughly 14,700 additional lines of new code, tests, schemas and dogfood assets.
- No current staged changes or commits for this tranche.

It adds or strengthens:

- Active sandbox-boundary probing, persisted as a signed observation and bound into the completion receipt.
- A trusted operator-capture helper for authenticating live fault-trial evidence.
- A passive recorder and declared oracles for the nine remaining live fault claims.
- Fail-closed, contained `verdict` execution.
- Stronger Graph/Campaign delegation authority.
- Durable ownership and recovery for merge-repair children.
- Campaign child crash adoption, cancellation and duplicate-launch prevention.
- Better supervisor-service status, boot identity and machine-restart evidence.
- An explicit `--untrusted` boundary for in-place and sandbox-none foreground execution.
- Crash-atomic, receipt-bound verified export with a journal, staging tree, backup, rollback and recovery.

The verified-export slice has focused tests passing, including all 86 lifecycle tests. However, the complete unstaged tranche has not yet been demonstrated to pass the full repository gate as one integrated state.

The tree also contains unrelated material that must not enter these commits: `.specstory` histories, IDE settings, Python caches and generated notes.

## What remains on the docket

In priority order:

1. Integrate the current tranche safely.

   Split it into dependency-ordered commits: trust foundation, sandbox containment, Job delegation/repair ownership, supervisor service, explicit untrusted routing, verified export, then dogfood/docs. Exclude session and generated files.

2. Run the full verification gate.

   The current working tree is too interconnected to call complete based only on focused tests. It needs formatting, compilation, unit/integration tests, adversarial suites and `make verify` after commit assembly.

3. Perform the actual dogfood campaign.

   The current live matrix records 2 attempted tasks, 22 not run and 0 verified. We still need the planned 20–30 tasks across multiple repositories and provider routes, measuring:

   - unattended completion;
   - recovery;
   - interventions;
   - false acceptance/rejection;
   - comprehension time;
   - worker and judge cost.

4. Prove real interruption recovery.

   Still unproven live:

   - an active launchd/systemd service;
   - a real machine reboot;
   - live supervisor and worker death;
   - network loss;
   - Campaign interruption and roll-up recovery;
   - naturally occurring semantic `revise`;
   - recovery during parent repair;
   - Linux/bubblewrap;
   - a complete strict Docker Job.

5. Resolve the remaining compatibility boundary.

   Historical `chain run|resume`, policy-rich chain modes, extension, previews and explicitly in-place/uncontained execution remain process-owned. We must either migrate them or deliberately retain/retire them as untrusted compatibility paths.

6. Only then consider expansion.

   Resource leases, rules-as-signed-input, MCP exposure and cross-machine scheduling remain useful follow-ups, but should not precede proving the local promise.

## Honest assessment of the promise

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done…

Implemented.

> It will work in isolation…

Implemented for supported strict Jobs, with fail-closed behavior when real containment is unavailable.

> Survive interruptions…

Implemented and hermetically tested for many crash windows; real machine-restart and several live-provider scenarios remain unproven.

> Stop for explicit bounded reasons…

Implemented.

> Independently verify both the checks and the meaning…

Implemented.

> Leave behind a clear receipt…

Implemented and cryptographically bound; the newest containment observation and export hardening are awaiting integration.

So we have built the kernel of the promised product. We have not yet earned the unconditional operational claim. The next move should be integration and live acceptance—not another broad feature expansion. The canonical current assessment is in [MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md:136), with the remaining drills in [WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md:561).

+#[test]
+fn unowned_legacy_merge_refuses_before_any_artifact_mutation() {
+    let temp = TempDir::new().expect("tempdir");
+    let workspace = temp.path().join("workspace");
+    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
+    fs::create_dir_all(&workspace).expect("workspace");
+
+    let mut plan = Plan::new(
+        "complete both legacy branches",
+        PlanMode::FullPlan,
+        vec![
+            PlanTask::new(0, "first", "complete first", PlanRole::Child, None),
+            PlanTask::new(1, "second", "complete second", PlanRole::Child, None),
+        ],
+        PlanProviders::default(),
+        Some("legacy-merge-test".to_string()),
+        "test",
+    )
+    .expect("legacy Plan");
+    plan.status = PlanStatus::Forked;
+    plan.parent_cwd = Some(workspace.clone());
+    for task in &mut plan.tasks {
+        task.status = PlanTaskStatus::Completed;
+    }
+    save_plan(&paths, &plan).expect("save legacy Plan");
+
+    let before = snapshot_tree(paths.home());
+    let output = deadreckon(&paths, &workspace)
+        .args([
+            "merge",
+            &plan.plan_id,
+            "--strategy",
+            "prefer-child",
+            "--prefer-child",
+            "999",
+            "--repair-provider",
+            "must-not-be-resolved",
+            "--quiet",
+            "--plain",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .expect("legacy merge");
+
+    assert_unowned_refusal(&output, "merge", "Plan");
+    assert_eq!(
+        snapshot_tree(paths.home()),
+        before,
+        "merge changed state, events, provider evidence, or result files before refusing"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn unowned_legacy_campaign_repair_refuses_before_any_artifact_mutation() {
+    let temp = TempDir::new().expect("tempdir");
+    let workspace = temp.path().join("workspace");
+    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
+    fs::create_dir_all(&workspace).expect("workspace");
+
+    let mut campaign = Campaign::new(
+        "complete both legacy campaign branches",
+        build_sub_goals(
+            vec!["complete first".to_string(), "complete second".to_string()],
+            2,
+        )
+        .expect("sub-goals"),
+        PlanProviders::default(),
+        0,
+        None,
+        None,
+        "test",
+    )
+    .expect("legacy Campaign");
+    campaign.status = CampaignStatus::Failed;
+    for (index, sub) in campaign.sub_goals.iter_mut().enumerate() {
+        sub.status = SubGoalStatus::Merged;
+        sub.result_run_id = Some(format!("{:032}", index + 1));
+        sub.scope = Some("legacy-campaign-test".to_string());
+    }
+    let campaign_dir = paths.plan_dir(&campaign.campaign_id);
+    fs::create_dir_all(&campaign_dir).expect("campaign dir");
+    write_campaign(&campaign_dir, &campaign).expect("write legacy Campaign");
+    let rollup = build_rollup(&campaign, |_| {
+        (
+            "signed".to_string(),
+            AcceptanceTamperVerdict::Clean,
+            Vec::new(),
+        )
+    });
+    write_campaign_rollup(&campaign_dir, &rollup).expect("write campaign roll-up");
+
+    let before = snapshot_tree(paths.home());
+    let output = deadreckon(&paths, &workspace)
+        .args([
+            "campaign",
+            "repair",
+            &campaign.campaign_id,
+            "--repair-mode",
+            "child",
+            "--repair-provider",
+            "must-not-be-resolved",
+            "--quiet",
+            "--plain",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .expect("legacy campaign repair");
+
+    assert_unowned_refusal(&output, "campaign repair", "Campaign");
+    assert_eq!(
+        snapshot_tree(paths.home()),
+        before,
+        "campaign repair changed state, events, provider evidence, or result files before refusing"
+    );
+}
+
+fn deadreckon(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, workspace: &Path) -> Command {
+    let mut command = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_deadreckon"));
+    command
+        .current_dir(workspace)
+        .env("DEADRECKON_HOME", paths.home());
+    command
+}
+
+fn assert_unowned_refusal(output: &Output, operation: &str, artifact_kind: &str) {
+    assert!(
+        !output.status.success(),
+        "stdout:\n{}\nstderr:\n{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+    );
+    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
+    assert!(stderr.contains(operation), "{stderr}");
+    assert!(stderr.contains(artifact_kind), "{stderr}");
+    assert!(stderr.contains("has no durable Job owner"), "{stderr}");
+    assert!(stderr.contains("deadreckon start"), "{stderr}");
+    assert!(!stderr.contains("--untrusted"), "{stderr}");
+}
+
+fn snapshot_tree(root: &Path) -> BTreeMap<PathBuf, Option<Vec<u8>>> {
+    fn visit(
+        root: &Path,
+        current: &Path,
+        snapshot: &mut BTreeMap<PathBuf, Option<Vec<u8>>>,
+    ) {
+        let mut entries = fs::read_dir(current)
+            .expect("read snapshot directory")
+            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
+            .expect("read snapshot entries");
+        entries.sort_by_key(fs::DirEntry::file_name);
+        for entry in entries {
+            let path = entry.path();
+            let relative = path
+                .strip_prefix(root)
+                .expect("snapshot path stays under root")
+                .to_path_buf();
+            let file_type = entry.file_type().expect("snapshot file type");
+            if file_type.is_dir() {
+                snapshot.insert(relative, None);
+                visit(root, &path, snapshot);
+            } else {
+                snapshot.insert(relative, Some(fs::read(&path).expect("snapshot file")));
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    let mut snapshot = BTreeMap::new();
+    if root.is_dir() {
+        visit(root, root, &mut snapshot);
+    }
+    snapshot
+}

---
name: review-against-the-working-sibling
description: Use when implementing or reviewing a feature or fix in a codebase that already contains a similar working capability — locate the known-good in-repo sibling, diff against it, and propose the minimal change to reach parity, naming the one intentional difference.
---

# Review Against the Working Sibling

Do not design behavior from scratch or judge it against abstract quality when a proven analog already exists in the repo. Find the closest working sibling, treat it as the spec, and make the new code match that pattern — calling out the single intended delta so the diff surface stays minimal.

## Steps

1. Before building or reviewing, ask "how do we already do this here?" and locate the closest working sibling — the existing button, handler, event, provider, route, or component that does the analogous job correctly.
2. Read the sibling and extract its pattern: structure, naming, where responsibility lives, how it wires up.
3. Frame the work as "make this match that, with one named difference." State the single intended delta explicitly (e.g. "same as the Save flow, but Publish instead of Preview at the end").
4. Diff the new/broken code against the sibling and propose the minimal change that restores pattern parity — not a freeform rewrite.
5. In review, make conformance the first question: "does this match the precedent?" Name the specific reference file/feature the new work must conform to.
6. If you must abandon an approach, pair the retreat with the constructive replacement — usually an already-working shape to mirror, never a speculative do-over.

## Verification

The change is right when it is structurally indistinguishable from its named sibling except for the one stated delta. If you cannot name the sibling and the delta, you have not grounded the work.

## Failure modes

- Inventing a fresh implementation when a working analog exists — it drifts from house conventions and is harder to review.
- Reviewing for abstract "quality" instead of "does it match how we already do it?".
- Carrying over template/sibling code without adapting the one part that must differ (the user catches lines that are "not sufficiently adapted").

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-05). Consolidates anchor-review-in-working-sibling, precedent-conformance-check, and abandon-only-toward-a-working-exemplar.

- validate supported policy at `crates/deadreckon/src/commands/chain/mod.rs:801-838`;
- compile ordered dependencies at `:1217-1261`;
- create one Graph Job and detach its supervisor at `:1264-1415`.

Current comparison:

- Public `chain run|resume` already matches the product rule by retirement. CLI and TUI call sites at `:264-321` and `:3161-3177` reach the refusal at `:1423-1450` before mutation or execution. Only the characterization binary reaches the legacy conductor at `:1452-1468`.
- Public `chain extend` remains inconsistent. Call sites at `:355-373` and `:3045-3053` mutate `chain.json` and append an event at `:3443-3513`, even though the resulting schedule cannot be publicly resumed.
- `redo --extend` has the same issue at `:3516-3641`.

Recommended minimal change: retire public legacy extension rather than auto-convert it.

Make extension match the existing run/resume refusal, with one intentional delta: construct the requested updated schedule in memory so the refusal’s migration command includes the new goal, but do not save the Chain or append an event. Retain mutation only in `deadreckon-characterization`.

Auto-conversion is unsafe because stored chains may contain semantics Graph Jobs deliberately refuse: more than six steps, manual apply, non-stack/squash policy, allowlists, continue-on-failure, custom circuit breakers, `sandbox none`, or non-HEAD bases (`:1115-1165`). Progressed chains also carry run IDs and applied SHAs that a fresh Graph Job cannot honestly adopt.

- Product run refusal: `crates/deadreckon/tests/chain.rs:146-175`.
- Characterization-only foreground behavior: `:1701-1750`.
- Graph Job contract: `commands/chain/mod.rs:4542-4633`.
- Current extension mutations: `tests/chain.rs:1853-1887`, `:3774-3795`, `:3851-3884`, and `:3953-3977`.

Add production tests proving:

1. A supported direct chain creates exactly one Graph Job and no legacy Chain.
2. `extend` and `redo --extend` leave legacy bytes/events unchanged, create no Job, and recommend a durable schedule containing the requested goal.

+        .current_dir(&repo)
+        .args([

+            "redo",
+            &chain.chain_id,
+            "--extend",
+            "replacement durable goal",

+        .output()
+        .expect("product chain redo extend");

+    assert!(

+    assert!(stderr.contains("state mutation: none"), "{stderr}");
+    assert!(stderr.contains("Recommended\ndeadreckon chain --yes"), "{stderr}");
+    assert!(stderr.contains("\"replacement durable goal\""), "{stderr}");
+    assert_eq!(
+        fs::read(paths.chain_json(&chain.chain_id)).expect("chain after"),
+        before
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        fs::read(paths.chain_events(&chain.chain_id)).expect("events after"),
+        existing_events
+    );
+    assert!(
+        !paths.jobs_dir().exists()
+            || fs::read_dir(paths.jobs_dir())
+                .expect("jobs")
+                .next()
+                .is_none()
+    );

name: diagnose-before-edit
description: Use when behavior is surprising, a fix failed, or the territory is unfamiliar — suspend edits, trace the end-to-end mechanism, and prove WHERE and WHY before changing any code.
---

# Diagnose Before Edit

When something is misbehaving or you are in unfamiliar code, do not patch the symptom. Impose a read-only gate: name and trace the mechanism first, locate the fault, and only edit once the cause is pinned to specific files. This mirrors the user's standing practice of fusing an explicit "don't write any code yet" constraint to a "help me understand how X works" demand.

## Steps

1. Treat a "step back", "don't change anything yet", "where does X happen", or "how does this work" cue (explicit or implied by a surprising bug) as a switch into read-only diagnosis. Do not edit code in this phase.
2. Trace the end-to-end mechanism and narrate it: where the value/behavior originates, every hop it takes, and where it finally renders or takes effect. Name the specific files and lines.
3. Localize the fault before proposing any fix. State which location(s) you suspect and the evidence for that localization — and check whether it could live in more than one place rather than assuming a single site.
4. State the causal chain explicitly and, when rejecting a candidate fix, supply a competing root-cause hypothesis rather than just trying again.
5. Propose how the fix will be verified, then wait for authorization before editing.
6. Only after the mechanism's home is pinned to concrete files, make the minimal change at that layer — never patch the layer where the symptom merely surfaced.

## Verification

Before editing, you should be able to answer, in writing: "The behavior is produced by `<file>:<lines>` because `<causal chain>`, and I will confirm the fix by `<observation/command>`." If you cannot, you have not finished diagnosing.

## Failure modes

- Patching the layer where the symptom appears (e.g. button-state code) when the real cause is elsewhere (a default selection upstream). The user rejects this with: "You got it wrong… the issue was not with the button states." Localize first.
- Jumping to a fix on the first plausible theory. Demand or construct the observation that would discriminate between candidate causes before committing to one.
- Editing during a "don't write any code yet" instruction. That instruction is a gate, not a delay — produce the mechanism trace and stop.

## Notes

Forged by Lore from latent practice across specstory-monorepo and stoa (2024-12 → 2026-04), consistently followed by the user, high adjacent-approval rate. Consolidates the read-before-write gate, fault-localization-before-fix, and mechanism-trace-before-trust patterns.

    24	/// Authenticate and atomically persist the latest controller-produced

    27	/// A prior regular observation may be replaced by a later attempt. Any

    29	pub fn seal_sandbox_boundary_observation(
    30	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    31	    state: &PipelineState,
    32	    authority: &JobAuthority,
    33	    observation: &SandboxBoundaryObservation,
    34	) -> Result<SandboxBoundaryObservation> {
    35	    validate_observation_fields(paths, state, authority, observation, None)?;
    36	    let mut sealed = observation.clone();
    37	    sealed.schema_version = JobSchemaVersion::CURRENT;
    38	    sealed.signature.clear();
    39	    let key = read_gate_key(paths, authority.job_id.as_ref())?;
    40	    sealed.signature = sign_observation(&sealed, &key)?;
    41	
    42	    let path = paths.job_sandbox_boundary_observation(authority.job_id.as_ref());
    43	    refuse_non_regular_existing_target(&path, authority.job_id.as_ref())?;
    44	    atomic_write_json(&path, &sealed)?;
    45	
    46	    let persisted =
    47	        validate_sandbox_boundary_observation(paths, state, authority, &sealed.sandbox_backend)?;
    48	    if persisted != sealed {
    49	        return Err(observation_error(
    50	            authority.job_id.as_ref(),
    51	            "persisted observation differs from the controller-produced bytes",
    52	        ));
    53	    }
    54	    Ok(sealed)
    55	}

## Conclusion

The strict native trust path is substantially implemented and coherent. The remaining Docker blocker is precise:

> DeadReckon proves that “a Docker boundary was exercised,” but it neither executes a guaranteed platform-compatible `dr-gate` nor proves which evaluator bytes produced the process-check results.

This is fail-safe today on macOS—it fails rather than falsely accepting—but it prevents a public strict Docker Job from completing and leaves a provenance gap on any platform where it happens to run.

### Current causal chain

1. Job creation freezes the goal, contract, policy, source tree, launch plan and requested sandbox in [job.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/job.rs:58) and [job.rs](crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/job.rs:101). No evaluator identity is frozen in `JobExecutionPolicy` or `JobAuthority` ([job.rs](crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/job.rs:319)).

2. The supervisor revalidates those frozen inputs before each attempt ([supervisor.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:1275)), records a fenced guarded launch ([supervisor.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:961)), and passes the approved sandbox plus attempt/launch identity to the worker ([supervisor.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:1570)).

3. When the worker reaches completion, it calls the deterministic gate ([turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:795), [turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:3791)). Strict Jobs require a real resolved backend and a durable launch owner ([turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2689)).

4. DeadReckon first runs a boundary probe. This probe is `/bin/sh`, not `dr-gate` ([turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2857), [turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2956)). It proves key, proof, control and environment denials, but not that the evaluator can execute.

5. `gate_binary_path()` merely chooses an existing sibling named `dr-gate`; it does not canonicalize, require a stable regular file, hash it or inspect its platform ([turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:4947)). It is resolved independently for the guarded helper, evaluator and signer ([turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2746), [turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2801), [turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:3086)).

6. Guarded launch correctly persists process identity before release and reaps residual descendants ([process.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/process.rs:25), [pid_file.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/exec/pid_file.rs:33)). Its durable identity contains attempt, launch, boot, PID and release-token data, but no evaluator digest ([pid_file.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/exec/pid_file.rs:41)).

7. Backend behavior diverges:

   - Seatbelt directly executes the native host `dr-gate` behind `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` ([commands.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs:71)).
   - Bubblewrap read-only binds host paths and executes the native Linux `dr-gate` at the same path ([commands.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs:94)).
   - Docker mounts the host gate directory into a `rust:1` Linux container and tries to execute the host path there. The image is a mutable tag, with no `--platform` or `--pull=never` ([commands.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs:185)).

   On this host, both built `dr-gate` binaries are Mach-O arm64. The installed `rust:1` image is Linux/arm64. Architecture matches; executable format does not. Therefore the shell boundary probe can pass and the real evaluator subsequently fails with an incompatible executable.

8. Evaluator output carries run, directory, contract, results and tamper facts, but no binary or platform identity ([gate.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:200)). This is security-relevant because the signer does not rerun cargo, build or shell checks. It validates their shape and claimed success suffix; only file/content results and tamper evidence are independently recomputed ([gate.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:786), [gate.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:876)).

9. After evaluator reaping, the controller reads the HMAC key and invokes a newly resolved host signer ([turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2788)). The marker authenticates checks, containment and backend, but not evaluator identity ([gate.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:91), [gate.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:1604)).

10. The signed sandbox observation binds attempt, authority, contract, result tree, probe and backend ([job.rs](crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/job.rs:426), [sandbox_observation.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/sandbox_observation.rs:101)). The completion receipt binds that observation and the two completion keys ([completion.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/completion.rs:130), [completion.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/completion.rs:222)), but neither names the evaluator.

The repository already states this accurately: the live Docker test proves only the common boundary, while a public strict Docker Job remains outstanding ([AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:4356)). The existing Docker test runs `/bin/sh`, not `dr-gate` ([lib.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/lib.rs:230)).

## Smallest trustworthy design

Freeze one versioned `GateToolchainIdentity` before the first agent turn:

- Controller binary digest and host OS/architecture.
- Evaluator binary digest and evaluator OS/architecture.
- Evaluator protocol/schema version.
- For Docker: immutable image ID or repository digest, explicit platform and fixed guest evaluator path.
- Digest of the complete identity manifest.

For native backends, copy the approved host `dr-gate` into a protected content-addressed evaluator store. Seatbelt executes that artifact; bubblewrap read-only binds the exact file, not merely its parent directory.

For Docker, use a preinstalled multi-architecture DeadReckon gate image containing the appropriate Linux `dr-gate`. Execute:

- the image by immutable digest;
- with explicit `--platform`;
- with `--pull=never`;
- at a fixed guest path.

Do not mount the macOS or Windows host evaluator into Linux.

The boundary probe should become a `dr-gate probe-boundary` mode. That makes the first probe prove both containment and actual evaluator compatibility. The subsequent evaluation must use the same pinned identity.

An evaluator-reported digest is useful for cross-layer correlation but is not the trust root—the trusted launcher’s pinned artifact or image is.

## Required insertion points

- Wire schemas and schema version: [job.rs](crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/job.rs:19), [job.rs](crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/job.rs:101), [job.rs](crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/job.rs:319), [job.rs](crates/deadreckon-protocol/src/job.rs:385).
- Freeze manifest/artifact before policy and authority hashing: [job.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/job.rs:112).
- Add protected evaluator paths: [paths.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:91), [policy.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/policy.rs:43).
- Revalidate manifest and artifact on every claimed attempt: [supervisor.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:1275).
- Carry manifest digest through launch events and guarded process records: [supervisor.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/supervisor.rs:985), [spec.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/spec.rs:9), [pid_file.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/exec/pid_file.rs:41).
- Resolve the identity once per gate, then reuse it for probe, evaluator and signer: [turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2689).
- Enforce backend-specific evaluator serialization at the final common boundary: [commands.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs:19).
- Replace the Docker tag/host-path execution: [commands.rs](crates/deadreckon-sandbox/src/commands.rs:185).
- Extend `dr-gate` modes and output: [dr-gate.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/bin/dr-gate.rs:18), [gate.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:200).
- Revalidate evaluator identity before the signing key is read: [turn_loop.rs](crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:2788), [gate.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:646).
- HMAC-bind identity into the marker, observation and receipt: [gate.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:1604), [sandbox_observation.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/sandbox_observation.rs:239), [completion.rs](crates/deadreckon-core/src/completion.rs:1620).
- Ensure graph and campaign parent gates use the same identity without a bypass: [graph_job.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/graph_job.rs:4657), [graph_job.rs](crates/deadreckon/src/commands/graph_job.rs:5039).
- Extend release packaging with a multiarch evaluator image. Linux release targets already exist in [release.yml](.github/workflows/release.yml:145).

If a frozen artifact or image later disappears, DeadReckon should stop once with an explicit evaluator-unavailable or evaluator-incompatible reason. It must not silently pull, substitute the current installation, or retry indefinitely.

## Verification plan

- Schema/HMAC tests: changing binary digest, platform, image digest or manifest digest invalidates authority, evaluation, marker, observation and receipt.
- Stable-file tests: reject symlinked, non-regular or changing evaluator artifacts.
- Command serialization tests:
  - Seatbelt executes the frozen native artifact.
  - Bubblewrap read-only binds the exact artifact.
  - Docker includes immutable image ID, `--platform`, `--pull=never` and fixed guest path, with no host `dr-gate` path or `rust:1` tag.
- Adversarial tests: fake `PATH`, replaced evaluator, tag drift, wrong architecture, wrong OS, forged evaluation JSON and signer replacement all fail before key access.
- Live public tests:
  - macOS Seatbelt parity.
  - Linux bubblewrap parity.
  - macOS and Linux strict Docker Job reaching a valid marker, semantic judgment and receipt.
  - Kill the worker during probe/evaluation and confirm reaping plus recovery using the same frozen identity.
  - Remove the pinned image after approval and confirm an explicit bounded stop with no pull.
- Release test: each advertised Docker platform runs its packaged `dr-gate`, and the released image/binary digests match the manifest frozen into a Job.

The native implementation provides the right skeleton. The remaining work is not a new scheduler or proof system; it is closing one identity chain from Job approval to the exact evaluator bytes that supplied the non-recomputed process-check results.

+fn validate_gate_evaluator_binding(
+    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
+    authority: &JobAuthority,
+    observation: &SandboxBoundaryObservation,
+) -> Result<()> {
+    let job_id = authority.job_id.as_ref();
+    let job = crate::load_job(paths, job_id)?;
+    let policy_identity = job
+        .policy
+        .execution
+        .as_ref()
+        .and_then(|execution| execution.gate_evaluator.as_ref());
+    match (
+        policy_identity,
+        authority.gate_evaluator_sha256.as_deref(),
+        observation.gate_evaluator_sha256.as_deref(),

+        (None, None, None) => Ok(()),
+        (Some(identity), Some(authority_digest), Some(observation_digest)) => {
+            validate_gate_evaluator_identity(
+                identity,

+                &observation.sandbox_backend,
+                job_id,
+            )?;
+            let actual = gate_evaluator_identity_sha256(identity)?;
+            require_digest(
+                authority_digest,
+                &actual,
+                job_id,
+                "approved gate evaluator identity",
+            )?;
+            require_digest(
+                observation_digest,
+                &actual,
+                job_id,
+                "observed gate evaluator identity",
+            )?;
+            Ok(())
+        }
+        _ => Err(observation_error(
+            job_id,
+            "gate evaluator identity is partial across policy, authority, and observation",
+        )),
+    }
+}

+fn validate_gate_evaluator_identity(
+    identity: &GateEvaluatorIdentity,

+) -> Result<()> {
+    if identity.schema_version != GATE_EVALUATOR_IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION
+        || identity.protocol_version != GATE_EVALUATOR_PROTOCOL_VERSION

+        || !valid_binary_identity(&identity.evaluator)

+        return Err(observation_error(
+            job_id,
+            "gate evaluator identity version, protocol, or binary identity is invalid",
+        ));
+    }
+
+    let requested_docker = sandbox_requested == "docker";
+    let observed_docker = sandbox_backend == "docker";
+    if requested_docker != observed_docker {
+        return Err(observation_error(
+            job_id,
+            "Docker evaluator identity does not match the requested and observed backend",
+        ));
+    }
+    match identity.docker.as_ref() {
+        None if observed_docker => Err(observation_error(
+            job_id,
+            "Docker verification is missing its immutable image identity",
+        )),
+        Some(_) if !observed_docker => Err(observation_error(
+            job_id,
+            "native verification unexpectedly carries a Docker evaluator identity",
+        )),
+        None => {
+            if identity.controller != identity.evaluator {

+                    "native verification controller and evaluator identities differ",
+                ));
+            }
+            Ok(())
+        }
+        Some(docker) => {
+            if identity.evaluator.os != "linux"

+                || docker.guest_path != Path::new(DOCKER_GATE_GUEST_PATH)
+                || !docker_platform_matches_binary(

+                ));

+        }
+    }
+}
+
+fn valid_binary_identity(identity: &GateBinaryIdentity) -> bool {
+    valid_sha256(&identity.sha256)
+        && valid_platform_component(&identity.os)
+        && valid_platform_component(&identity.arch)
+}
+
+fn valid_platform_component(value: &str) -> bool {
+    !value.is_empty()
+        && value.bytes().all(|byte| {
+            byte.is_ascii_lowercase()
+                || byte.is_ascii_digit()
+                || matches!(byte, b'_' | b'-' | b'.')
+        })
+}
+
+fn docker_platform_matches_binary(platform: &str, os: &str, arch: &str) -> bool {
+    let Some((platform_os, platform_arch)) = platform.split_once('/') else {
+        return false;
+    };
+    !platform_arch.contains('/')
+        && platform_os == os
+        && normalized_arch(platform_arch) == normalized_arch(arch)
+}
+
+fn normalized_arch(arch: &str) -> &str {
+    match arch {
+        "aarch64" => "arm64",
+        "x86_64" => "amd64",
+        other => other,
+    }
+}

fn hex_decode(value: &str) -> std::result::Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    if !value.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
        return Err("odd length".to_string());
    }
    value
        .as_bytes()
        .chunks_exact(2)
        .map(|pair| {
            let high = hex_nibble(pair[0])?;
            let low = hex_nibble(pair[1])?;
            Ok((high << 4) | low)
        })
        .collect()
}

fn hex_nibble(value: u8) -> std::result::Result<u8, String> {
    match value {
        b'0'..=b'9' => Ok(value - b'0'),
        b'a'..=b'f' => Ok(value - b'a' + 10),
        b'A'..=b'F' => Ok(value - b'A' + 10),
        _ => Err("non-hex character".to_string()),
    }
}

fn observation_error(job_id: &str, detail: &str) -> DeadreckonError {
    DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
        "sandbox boundary observation for {job_id} is invalid: {detail}"
    ))

pub fn task_key(goal: &str) -> String {
    let trimmed = goal.trim();
    let mut stem = sanitize_slug(trimmed);
    if stem.len() > 48 {
        stem.truncate(48);
        stem = stem.trim_end_matches('-').to_string();
    }
    if stem.is_empty() {
        stem = "task".to_string();
    }
    format!("{stem}-{:08x}", fnv1a32(trimmed))
}

pub fn sanitize_slug(input: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len());
    let mut last_dash = false;
    for ch in input.chars() {
        let next = if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
            last_dash = false;
            Some(ch.to_ascii_lowercase())
        } else if matches!(ch, '-' | '_' | ' ' | '.') {
            if last_dash {
                None
            } else {
                last_dash = true;
                Some('-')
            }
        } else {
            None
        };
        if let Some(ch) = next {
            out.push(ch);
        }
    }
    out.trim_matches('-').to_string()
}

fn operator_capture_component(value: &str) -> String {
    let mut output = String::with_capacity(value.len().max(1));
    for byte in value.as_bytes() {
        if byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(*byte, b'-' | b'_') {
            output.push(char::from(*byte));
        } else {
            output.push('%');
            output.push_str(&format!("{byte:02x}"));
        }
    }
    if output.is_empty() {
        "%00".to_string()
    } else {
        output
    }
}

fn find_git_root(start: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut cursor = if start.is_file() {
        start.parent()?.to_path_buf()
    } else {
        start.to_path_buf()
    };
    loop {
        if cursor.join(".git").exists() {
            return Some(cursor);
        }
        if !cursor.pop() {
            return None;
        }
    }
}

fn fnv1a32(input: &str) -> u32 {
    let mut hash = 0x811c_9dc5u32;
    for byte in input.as_bytes() {
        hash ^= u32::from(*byte);
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193);
    }
    hash
}
